overview.description: Russian Bank is a competitive patience game for two players, played with two standard 52-card packs (one per player). Each player has a reserve, hand, and waste pile; they build eight shared foundations (Ace to King by suit) and an eight-column tableau in descending alternating colors, and may load cards onto the opponent's reserve or waste. First to play off all cards wins; opponents may call Stop on an illegal or omitted compulsory move.

setup.dealing: Each player shuffles the other's pack. Each deals from own pack: 12 face-down + 1 face-up (reserve), 4 face-up in a column above reserve (houses). Thirty-five cards remain as hand. Space between tableau columns for eight foundation piles.

rules.objective: Be the first player to get rid of all cards from your hand, waste pile, and reserve by playing them to the eight foundations (Ace to King same suit), the eight tableau houses (descending alternating colors), or by loading onto the opponent's reserve or waste (same suit, adjacent rank). Opponent may call Stop on an illegal or omitted compulsory move.
rules.gameplay:
1. Setup: Each player shuffles the other's pack; each deals 12 face-down and one face-up (reserve), 4 face-up tableau cards (houses), and holds 35 cards (hand). Space between columns for eight foundation piles.
2. First player: Lower top reserve card (K high, A low) starts; if equal, compare house cards.
3. Turn: Play available cards (reserve top, tableau outermost, then hand card when no compulsory moves)—to foundations (Ace then same-suit ascending), tableau (descending alternating color), or load onto opponent's reserve/waste (same suit, rank ±1). Compulsory: reserve to foundation first; any available to foundation; fill empty tableau from reserve before turning hand card. Opponent may call Stop on violation; undo move and opponent plays.
4. End: First with no hand, reserve, or waste wins. Stalemate: lower remaining count wins (hand/waste 1 each, reserve 2 each).
keyRules: Reserve card to foundation takes priority; then any available to foundation; fill tableau from reserve before turning hand
Building: foundations same suit ascending; tableau descending alternating colors; load opponent same suit adjacent rank
Call Stop on illegal move or omitted compulsory move; offender undoes and loses turn

strategy.basic: Use reserve and tableau cards to foundations before turning a hand card; fill empty tableau spaces from reserve when possible; load onto opponent's reserve or waste to block them.
strategy.intermediate: Plan order of plays to satisfy compulsory moves while maximizing options; prefer moves that expose new reserve or tableau cards.
strategy.advanced: Track which cards are in opponent's hand and waste; time loading onto opponent to maximize their dead cards; avoid leaving tableau cards that only you can use.
tips: Reserve-to-foundation has highest priority; never turn a hand card while a compulsory move exists.
Call Stop as soon as the opponent violates a priority or makes an illegal move.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy identification.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where each rank has distinct value and meaning depending on the specific game rules and player strategies.

scoring.description: Winner scores 30 points plus 1 per card left in opponent's hand and waste piles, plus 2 per card left in opponent's reserve. Stalemate: player with lower remaining count scores the difference (no 30-point bonus). Agreed target (e.g. 300) wins the match.
scoring.winCondition: First player to play off all cards from hand, reserve, and waste pile wins the game; first to reach agreed target score (e.g. 300) wins the match.
